exposure: causes of death (hypertensive disease, circulatory system disease, neoplasms, coagulopathies, post-abortion infection)
cohort: Women who experienced maternal mortality in a city in the North of Minas Gerais, Brazil, between 2009 and 2013.
finding: Maternal mortality in the studied city predominantly affected women aged 20-34, of mixed race, single, with low schooling, with most deaths being direct obstetric and likely avoidable, and a higher occurrence was found in areas of medium to high social vulnerability.
mod_finding: 68.1% of the maternal deaths occurred in women who underwent cesarean childbirth.
